- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to align with volatility decay.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture sentiment-driven rebound.  
- Model underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — add 0.5–1.5% to short-term forecast to account for lag.  
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to smooth out extremes; use sentiment-weighted average to avoid over-smoothing during sharp swings.  
- In high-sentiment volatility periods (e.g., sentiment std > 0.3), model often underpredicts peak prices — increase forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 day horizon to capture momentum.
